_legend: status: READ = numbers read in the fetched source text/table (local copy in papers/ or the .osim); COMPUTED = produced by moment_arms.py / scenarios.py from the .osim geometry; NOT_ACCESSIBLE = paywalled / not read (nothing quoted from it). No from-memory numbers are used.

sources.cite: gait2392_thelen2003muscle.osim (OpenSim 4.0 file; Delp et al. 1990 IEEE TBME 37:757 lineage; model geometry NOT re-read from the 1990 paper)
Rajagopal A, Dembia CL, DeMers MS, Delp DD, Hicks JL, Delp SL. Full-body musculoskeletal model for muscle-driven simulation of human gait. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2016;63:2068-79
sources.status: READ (Table II, Eq. 2-3 and text, PMC XML; and Rajagopal2016.osim)

numbers.method: F = 60 N/cm2 * muscle_volume_fraction(Handsfield 2014) * V_total / l_opt; V_total = 47*m*h + 1285 (m=75 kg, h=1.70 m); l_opt / pennation from Ward 2009 (cadaver)

sources.cite: RajagopalLaiUhlrich2023.osim (Lai/Uhlrich release of the Rajagopal model)
sources.numbers: hip/knee geometry of iliacus, psoas, rectus femoris identical to Rajagopal2016; vasti wrap/geometry slightly different

sources.cite: Arnold EM, Ward SR, Lieber RL, Delp SL. A model of the lower limb for analysis of human movement. Ann Biomed Eng 2010;38:269-79
sources.status: READ (Table 1 and Results text, PMC XML)

numbers.text_knee_extension_moment_arm: model peaked at 4.7 cm at 25 deg knee flexion; other data (refs 14,18,40) suggest peak quadriceps knee-extension moment arm is approximately 4-5 cm

sources.cite: Ward SR, Eng CM, Smallwood LH, Lieber RL. Are current measurements of lower extremity muscle architecture accurate? Clin Orthop Relat Res 2009;467:1074-82
sources.status: READ (architecture table + joint-group table, PMC HTML)

sources.cite: Kumazaki T, Takahashi T, et al. Action and contribution of the iliopsoas and rectus femoris as hip flexor agonists examined with anatomical analysis. Juntendo Iji Zasshi 2022;68(4):352-362, doi:10.14789/jmj.JMJ22-0009-OA
sources.status: READ (abstract, methods, results, tables; 22 fixed Japanese cadaver limbs, age ~79)

numbers.MAL_RF_max_mm: 50.4 at hip 40 deg (straight line AIIS to tibial tuberosity, sagittal projection)
numbers.iliopsoas_MAL_assumption: femoral-head radius for hip angles up to 50-60 deg (muscle assumed to wrap the head), then perpendicular distance to the straight line

RF_share_of_PM+IL+RF_torque_indicator_PC.note: falls behind iliopsoas at ~60-70 deg, iliopsoas dominates at 80-90 deg; only PM, IL, RF counted (no sartorius/TFL/adductors)

sources.cite: Jiroumaru T, et al. Measurement of muscle length-related electromyography activity of the hip flexor muscles to determine individual muscle contributions to the hip flexion torque. SpringerPlus 2014;3:624, doi:10.1186/2193-1801-3-624
sources.status: READ (abstract, results; 10 young men, sEMG, MVIC at knee 90 deg)

numbers.EMG_result: normalised RMS of TFL (0.81 at 30, 0.66 at 60) and sartorius (0.62 at 60) fell vs 0 deg; iliopsoas and RF RMS not significantly changed; authors conclude iliopsoas contribution is relatively larger in the flexed position (qualitative, no share numbers)

sources.cite: Herzog W, Read LJ. Lines of action and moment arms of the major force-carrying structures crossing the human knee joint. J Anat 1993;182:213-230
sources.status: NOT_ACCESSIBLE (scanned pages; only the abstract was read, which gives no numbers) - nothing quoted

sources.cite: Handsfield GG et al. Relationships of 35 lower limb muscles to height and body mass quantified using MRI. J Biomech 2014;47:631-8 (PMID 24368144)
sources.status: NOT_ACCESSIBLE (not in PMC, publisher paywalled). Its volume fractions enter only through the Rajagopal 2016 forces (derived volumes above, COMPUTED).
